title: Adaptive request thinning with per-session KV checkpoints and model downshift
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Transient OOMs caused by bursty request patterns and long-lived KV states lead to hard failures and poor latency tail. Existing mitigations (aggressive eviction, model fallbacks) either disrupt user sessions or lose semantic state. Goal: implement an orchestration layer that 1) reduces incoming memory pressure via adaptive request thinning/admission, 2) preserves user-visible context using lightweight per-session KV checkpoints, and 3) enables fast, stateful model downshift to smaller/quantized variants with graceful resume when capacity returns.
proposal_outline: 1) Admission controller: a stream-aware request-thinning policy that considers per-GPU headroom, current batching window, and session criticality tags. Thinning is probabilistic with backpressure hints delivered to clients when available. 2) KV checkpoints: periodic, incremental snapshots of session KV (diff-based) stored in a compact in-memory checkpoint store (LRU + size-bucketed). Checkpoints let us evict live KV and later restore without full re-computation. 3) Model downshift: coordinate a downshift path that swaps to a preloaded quantized micro-model on the same GPU when headroom drops below threshold. Use checkpoints to reconstruct minimal prefix state on the micro-model; stream tokens resume at lower fidelity and optionally re-request higher-fidelity regeneration async.
implementation_steps: - Phase A (PoC): implement lightweight checkpoint format + API (serialize delta of KV top N keys). Instrument memory accounting and simulate admission policy in the runtime test harness. - Phase B: integrate probabilistic thinning into the batch admission pipeline, add checkpoints eviction/restore hooks. Build downshift orchestration and test with end-to-end micro-model fallback. - Phase C: production hardening (metrics, Canary rollouts, safety timeouts, telemetry for SLO/quality drift), add canary auto-revert if quality drops beyond threshold.
data_structures_and_formats: Checkpoint entry fields are: session_id, seq_id, timestamp, keys[], compressed_values_blob (zstd), metadata (approx_size, token_offsets). All serialized blobs are stored in the existing cache store with tier tags (hot/warm). Admission controller exposes headroom estimate and probabilistic_rate per pool via /internal/admission. Downshift manifest maps canonical model -> [micro_model_variant, expected_prefix_loss_estimate].
api_changes: New internal endpoints: POST /internal/checkpoint/create, GET /internal/checkpoint/restore, GET /internal/admission/state. Client-visible: optional backpressure header X-Redwood-Thin: <expected_delay_ms> when thinning applied. Runtime config flags: checkpoint_interval_ms, checkpoint_max_per_session, downshift_headroom_threshold_mb.
metrics_and_slas: Track OOMs/sec, graceful-degradation-rate (requests served on micro-model), restore_success_rate, avg_restore_latency, token-cost delta when downshifted, user-visible quality regression (eval set) and P99 latency. SLO target: reduce hard OOMs by >=90% for bursty workloads while keeping median quality regression <2% on synthetic eval prompts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint serialization, integration e2e with synthetic bursty traffic (varying seq lengths), canary against 10% traffic with detailed A/B quality evals and regression alerts enabled. Fault injection: simulate checkpoint store eviction and force restore failures to validate graceful fallback (deny with 503 vs degrade path).
rollback_and_risk: If downshift causes unacceptable quality regressions, runtime supports immediate model-swap revert and marking sessions for offline replay. Risk: checkpointing adds write amplification and requires tight memory cap; mitigations include rate-limiting checkpoints and size buckets. Also monitor increased tail latency during restore; use soft timeouts to return degraded but fast response.
deliverables: - runtime: admission controller, checkpoint store, downshift orchestration - console: per-pool headroom dashboard and graceful-degradation metrics - docs: operational runbook and runbook playbook for OOM incidents - canary plan with rollback criteria
